nodes.summary: In a $(\lambda, \mu)$-smooth game with player set $I$, every $\varepsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium (additive error $\varepsilon$) $\sigma$ satisfies for every profile $t$. For $\mu < 1$ and $\varepsilon = 0$ this is $\mathbb E_\sigma[C] \le \frac{\lambda}{1 - \mu}\, C(t)$: price-of-anarchy bounds proved by smoothness hold for coarse correlated equilibria, not only for Nash equilibria.

nodes.summary: Suppose $T \ge 1$ rounds of a finite game are played and every player's regret against every fixed strategy is at most $T\varepsilon$. Then the empirical distribution of play is an $\varepsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium.

nodes.summary: In a finite strategic game with costs $c_i$, a probability distribution $\sigma$ on strategy profiles is an $\varepsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium (with additive error $\varepsilon$) if no player can lower its expected cost by more than $\varepsilon$ by committing in advance to a fixed strategy: for every player $i$ and every strategy $a \in S_i$. For $\varepsilon = 0$ these contain the correlated equilibria,…
nodes.title: Coarse correlated equilibrium

nodes.summary: For $T \ge 1$ rounds, the empirical distribution of play is a probability distribution on profiles.
nodes.title: The empirical distribution is a distribution

nodes.summary: A function $\mu$ on the finite set of strategy profiles is a probability distribution if $\mu(s) \ge 0$ for every profile $s$ and $\sum_s \mu(s) = 1$.
nodes.title: Distribution on strategy profiles

nodes.summary: A cost-minimisation game is $(\lambda, \mu)$-smooth if for every two profiles $s$ and $t$. For $\mu < 1$ this implies that every pure Nash equilibrium costs at most $\lambda / (1 - \mu)$ times every profile, the robust price-of-anarchy bound.
nodes.title: Smooth game

nodes.summary: The $k$-th coordinate of the expected regret vector of the weights $q$ against $b$ is $\sum_a q(a)\,c(a, b) - \bigl(\sum_a q(a)\bigr) c(k, b)$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the expected regret vector

nodes.summary: The coordinatewise negative part $(\min(x_k, 0))_k$ of a vector of $\mathbb R^A$; it is the nearest point of the nonpositive orthant.
nodes.title: Negative part of a vector

nodes.summary: The distance from $x$ to the nonpositive orthant is $\|x^+\| = \|x - \min(x, 0)\|$: the negative part is a nearest point, since $|x_k - y_k| \ge x_k^+$ for every $y_k \le 0$.
nodes.title: Distance to the nonpositive orthant

nodes.summary: The set $\{y \in \mathbb R^A : y_k \le 0 \text{ for all } k\}$, the target set for the regret vectors: a history has no positive average regret exactly when its average regret vector lies in it.
nodes.title: Nonpositive orthant

nodes.summary: The coordinatewise positive part $x^+ = (\max(x_k, 0))_k$ of a vector of $\mathbb R^A$.
nodes.title: Positive part of a vector

nodes.summary: For a decision maker with finite action set $A$ and costs $c(a, b)$ against the opponent's action $b$, the regret vector of having played $a$ against $b$ has coordinates $c(a, b) - c(k, b)$, $k \in A$: the cost saved by playing $k$ instead. Its average over the rounds is the vector of signed unconditional regrets $\tilde V(k) - U$ of Hart (2005), in cost form.
nodes.title: Regret vector

nodes.summary: The regret of player $i$ against the fixed strategy $a$ over the rounds $s^1, \dots, s^T$ is how much better $i$ would have done by playing $a$ in every round while the others played as they did. A no-regret algorithm keeps the maximum over $a$ of this quantity in $o(T)$ against every sequence of opponents' play.
nodes.title: Regret against a fixed strategy

nodes.summary: The social cost of a profile $s$ is $C(s) = \sum_i c_i(s)$, the total cost of the players.
nodes.title: Social cost

nodes.summary: $x - \min(x, 0) = x^+$ coordinatewise.
nodes.title: A vector minus its negative part

nodes.summary: For every function $g$ on profiles, $\sum_s \mu(s)\, g(s) = \frac1T \sum_{t=1}^T g(s^t)$ when $\mu$ is the empirical distribution of the rounds $s^1, \dots, s^T$: expectations under it are time averages.
nodes.title: Expectations under the empirical distribution

nodes.summary: The probabilities of unconditional regret matching add up to $1$.
nodes.title: Regret-matching probabilities add up to one

nodes.summary: The probabilities of unconditional regret matching are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Regret-matching probabilities are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Given the average regret vector $x$, unconditional regret matching plays each action $k$ with probability $x_k^+ / \sum_l x_l^+$, proportional to the positive part of its regret, and uniformly when no regret is positive (where Hart leaves the choice arbitrary).
nodes.title: Unconditional regret matching

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
